content.value_statement: Concurrent Go code can leak goroutines, deadlock, or mishandle cancellation. This skill provides production patterns for worker pools, pipelines, synchronization, and graceful shutdown.
actual_capabilities: Explains goroutines, channels, select statements, mutexes, wait groups, and context cancellation.
Designs worker pools with bounded concurrency, explicit channel ownership, and result collection.
Builds fan-out and fan-in pipelines with cancellation-aware stages.
Applies semaphores and errgroup limits to control concurrent workloads.
Reviews graceful shutdown flows using signals, contexts, timeouts, and wait groups.
Identifies common race, deadlock, channel, and goroutine lifecycle risks.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples but does not execute, compile, benchmark, or test Go programs.
Its examples require adaptation for application-specific workloads, latency targets, and failure policies.
It does not replace race-detector runs, load tests, profiling, or production monitoring.
Some examples depend on external Go modules that must be added to the project.

use_cases.title: Build a Worker Pool
use_cases.description: Create a bounded worker pool with cancellation, result handling, and clear channel ownership.
use_cases.target_user: Go developers adding parallel job processing

use_cases.title: Review Concurrent Services
use_cases.description: Assess goroutine lifecycles, shutdown behavior, synchronization, and error propagation before release.

use_cases.title: Debug Race Conditions
use_cases.description: Trace likely races, deadlocks, blocked channels, and leaks, then define focused verification steps.
use_cases.target_user: Site reliability engineers investigating production failures

prompt_templates.title: Explain Channel Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how buffered and unbuffered Go channels differ, including blocking behavior and one practical example for each.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn the foundations of channel communication.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Worker Pool
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a cancellable Go worker pool for [job type] with [worker count] workers, bounded queues, result collection, and clear channel ownership.
prompt_templates.scenario: Add controlled parallel processing to an application.

prompt_templates.title: Review Concurrency Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this concurrent Go design for goroutine leaks, deadlocks, races, and cancellation gaps, then propose focused fixes and verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate an existing implementation before release.

prompt_templates.title: Architect a Production Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Architect a Go pipeline for [workload] with fan-out, fan-in, backpressure, errgroup cancellation, graceful shutdown, and race-detector validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a complex concurrent service with operational safeguards.

output_examples.input: Design a five-worker image processing queue that stops cleanly when the request is canceled.
output: Use one producer-owned jobs channel and five workers that select on jobs and cancellation.
Close the results channel only after every worker exits through a wait group.
Return promptly on cancellation and record incomplete jobs for retry.

output_examples.input: Review a pipeline where a downstream consumer can return early.
output: The upstream sender can block forever after the consumer exits.
Pass one shared context through every stage and select on cancellation during each send.
Cancel the context on the first error and wait for all stages.

output_examples.input: Suggest a verification plan for a suspected race in a shared cache.
output: Run focused tests with the race detector under repeated concurrent reads and writes.
Check every shared field for consistent mutex ownership or replace suitable access with sync.Map.
Add stress tests that exercise deletion, replacement, cancellation, and shutdown.

best_practices: Give every goroutine a defined owner, exit condition, and cancellation path.
Close channels from the sending side and document which component owns closure.
Validate concurrent behavior with race detection, stress tests, timeouts, and representative load.
anti_patterns: Do not use sleeps to coordinate goroutines or assume scheduler ordering.
Do not launch unbounded goroutines for input that can grow without limit.
Do not ignore context cancellation during blocking sends, receives, or external operations.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete Go programs?
faq.answer: It can propose complete examples, but each design requires adaptation, compilation, testing, and review in your project.

faq.question: Can it detect data races automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can identify likely risks and recommend tests, but the Go race detector must evaluate running code.

faq.question: When should I use channels instead of mutexes?
faq.answer: Use channels for ownership transfer and coordination. Use mutexes when several goroutines must protect shared state directly.

faq.question: Does it cover graceful shutdown?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers signal handling, context cancellation, worker completion, channel closure, and shutdown timeouts.

faq.question: Does it support bounded concurrency?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes worker pools, channel semaphores, weighted semaphores, and errgroup limits.

faq.question: What validation should follow its recommendations?
faq.answer: Run unit tests, race detection, stress tests, benchmarks, profiling, and shutdown tests under representative load.
